page: Amazon Web Services c4.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the Xen hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor running at 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 25 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 15.0 GB, providing an allocation of 1.88 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c4.2xlarge predominantly within the average range across standard CPU and memory evaluations. The instance recorded 1470.98 on stress-ng single-core tests and 7763.44 on multi-core tests. Geekbench evaluations yielded 1182.0 for single-core and 4493.0 for multi-core performance, while PassMark reported an overall CPU score of 8431.71. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 50.6 GB/sec alongside 37.86 GB/sec write bandwidth. However, throughput drops were observed in memory-intensive operations: multi-threaded bzip3 decompression placed in the bottom 25% at 28.83 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput registered at 3.14 million operations per second.

Because of its compute-dense configuration with a lean memory profile, the c4.2xlarge provides solid resource efficiency for workloads bound primarily by CPU cycles rather than large RAM pools. Its 6.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 7015.0 clang compilation score indicate suitable operational efficiency for continuous integration build runners, batch processing, static web serving, and worker nodes in distributed compute systems.
